calculation_notes: The configured relative CFO bound is (RF_Hz × shift_ppm + nominal_IF_Hz × base_ppm) × 1e-6 divided by the minimum relative audio-clock ratio. At 5.8 GHz this is about 0.58 Hz; at 500 kHz it is about 50.15 microhertz.

The static frequency study requires the block-center CFO prior to remain strictly below 1/(2 × block_duration). It defaults to a frequency grid step 1/(4 × observation_duration); next-power-of-two FFT estimates apply that grid-shape rule and the full configured static CFO prior.

At 5.8 GHz, a 0.8-second block meets the CFO Nyquist condition but 81.1 million blocks exceed the static study 2^26 FFT cap; the finer 1/(4T) step requests 2^29. The 500 kHz example can use 8192-second blocks and fits a 2^15 static grid under the same model, subject to the other memory/work limits.

Two hertz is a capture-rate example because it exceeds twice the 0.58-Hz deterministic bound plus the modeled narrowband occupancy; 1 Hz fails the configure-mode deterministic capture check at 5.8 GHz.
At 2 samples/s, a 750-day raw export exceeds the CLI 128-million-row cap at both RF centers. This is an export limit, separate from streaming simulation and the static-study block/FFT limits.

These are current model, sampling, and implementation-resource constraints. They do not establish a physical link failure or a general impossibility: another acquisition architecture may avoid retaining all block projections or searching a uniform full-span CFO grid.

Configure-mode finite full-prior grid estimates at this 750-day duration are 300,895,874 frequency positions for 5.8 GHz and 26,019 for 500 kHz (about 11,561x). These are estimates, not materialized search banks or measured acquisition runtime.
